newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: POSSIBILITY OF ANOTHER OFFICIAL RATE CUT LOOMS
A slight rise in the official unemployment rate to 8.8 percent has prompted speculation that the Reserve Bank will again cut official interest rates.
Figures out today show an extra 40,000 people joined the ranks of the unemployed last month, despite a fall in the participation rate.
Senior economist with BT Australia, Rory Robertson, says these figures, and other recent economic indicators, demonstrate how difficult it is for the economy to improve.
Mr Robertson says economic data remains weak, and the market is putting immense pressure on the Reserve to again lower rates.
Meanwhile, the Federal Opposition's employment spokesman, Martin Ferguson, says the rise in the jobless rate shows how badly the Government is failing unemployed people.
Mr Ferguson says it appears as if some sections of the community are giving up hope.
He says the Prime Minister needs to show leadership if the hard decisions on policies to encourage employment growth are to be made.
BEAZLEY SAYS PM MUST GUARANTEE NEWCASTLE'S FUTURE
The Federal Opposition Leader, Kim Beazley, has told a rally of workers in Newcastle it is Prime Minister John Howard's job to demand BHP continues steel-making in the city.

Mr Beazley, New South Wales Premier Bob Carr and ACTU leader, Jennie George, have told workers pressure has to be maintained on BHP and the Federal Government to ensure a future for manufacturing in the region.
BHP workers marched on the steelworks after the rally.
Mr Beazley says its the Prime Minister's duty to ensure the future of manufacturing in Newcastle.
MOORE: EFFORT REQUIRED TO COMBAT RACIST TAG FOR AUSTRALIA
The Federal Government has backed a call for the tourism industry to take action to counteract damage to Australia's reputation caused by the racism debate.
The Australian Tourist Commission believes comments by Independent MP, Pauline Hanson, will have negative long-term effects on how Australia is perceived, especially in Asia.

Tourism Minister, John Moore, says the Government has made clear its position on Pauline Hanson's views, and it is up to all Australians to reinforce the nation's image as a friendly and welcoming country.
Mr Moore has also accused some Asian interests of capitalising on the race debate in Australia.
He says it sometimes pays Australia's competition as a tourist destination to play-up perceived racism in Australia.
SEARCH FOR KERRY WHELAN HOMES IN ON NATIONAL PARK
The search for clues to the disappearance of Kerry Whelan is focusing on an old mining area in the New South Wales southern highlands.
The 39-year-old vanished from a carpark in Parramatta more than five weeks ago.
Police say the search of the Morton National Park is in extremely rugged and dangerous terrain.
So far today, nothing of value has been found.
Tomorrow, police will start searching the 60 abandoned mines in the area, and police divers have been placed on stand-by.
LESSONS FROM BLACKHAWK COLLISION WILL "MAKE ARMY MORE RESILIENT"
The chief of the army says the Blackhawk helicopter disaster is a reminder of the dangers faced by young Australians responsible for defending their country.
A memorial service in Canberra today marked the first anniversary of the collision near Townsville, which killed 18 servicemen flying a night-time anti-terrorism exercise.
The ceremony, at the Royal Military College Chapel, is one of several being held around the country.
Army chief Lieutenant General John Sanderson told the gathering there were many reasons not to forget the Blackhawk disaster.
He said it will be a constant reminder of the demands placed on military personnel both in training and in war.
Lieutenant General Sanderson said the memories and lessons may be hard, but they are lessons nevertheless which add to the resilience and strength of the Army.
CRICKET: BICHEL'S ASHES TOUR OVER
Fast bowler Andy Bichel's Ashes cricket tour has come to an end after a prolonged back injury, which has limited the Queenslander to bowling just five overs since the tour began.
The Australian selectors will not call for a replacement.
Bichel will remain in England on holiday with his wife, who arrived yesterday.
Coach, Geoff Marsh, has told Channel Seven Jason Gillespie is unlikely to play in the second test at Lords, saying his inclusion after having torn his hamstring, would be too risky.
